subject: Post-termination data transfer & certified wipe plan
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@acmecorp.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-termination data transfer & certified wipe plan

Hi David,

Thanks for the call this week. As we move toward finalizing the DPA redlines, Acme needs clarity on Redwood's post-termination data handling. Specifically we need:

- A step-by-step plan for exporting customer data (format, delivery mechanism, encryption in transit) and a guaranteed window to complete the export after termination.
- A certified deletion process for all copies of Acme data across live systems, backups, snapshots and long-term archives, with timelines and an example deletion certificate/manifest.
- Confirmation of where backups and replicas may exist (regions) and whether Redwood will delete EU-resident copies on request.

Please see the attached Acme redline for the post-termination section (ACME_Redline_PostTerm.pdf) — we've flagged the clauses that require explicit timelines and proof. Our security team prefers an SFTP/AS2 transfer to our EU bucket and deletion of backups within 30 days of successful transfer unless a legal hold is invoked.

Can you confirm Redwood's standard approach and identify any operational constraints we should expect?

Appreciate a clear timeline and whether Redwood can provide a signed deletion manifest.

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Legal & Privacy, Acme Corporation
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-termination data transfer & certified wipe plan

Sara —

Thanks for the clear redline and for outlining Acme's expectations. Quick summary of Redwood's proposed operational plan (see attached "Redwood_Proposed_DPA_Redline_20260514.docx" for clause-level language):

1) Export window: Redwood will produce an export of customer data in vendor-neutral JSON/CSV (as applicable) and make it available for transfer within 7 calendar days after termination notice, unless an active legal hold is present. For large datasets we will scope the transfer in the SOW and may support staged exports.

2) Transfer mechanism: We can support SFTP (FTPS), AWS S3 presigned URLs, and secure SFTP into an Acme-managed EU bucket. All exports will be encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+). We recommend using your SFTP endpoint; Redwood can also push to a pre-provisioned S3 bucket in eu-west-1 with customer-supplied credentials.

3) Certified deletion: For live systems, Redwood will perform data erasure and provide a signed deletion manifest within 30 days of confirmed successful transfer. For backups/snapshots, due to snapshot chaining and replication timelines, we propose deletion completion within 90 days after transfer completion. We will provide a manifest and audit logs showing the deletion operations and object tombstones.

4) Regional guarantees: We can commit to preventing cross-border restoration of Acme data post-termination and to onshore (EU) residency for exported copies if requested. However, full deletion from backup chains may require the 90-day window noted above.

5) Proof/evidence: Redwood will provide: (a) deletion manifest (file list + SHA256 hashes removed); (b) internal job ids and timestamps for the erase jobs; (c) an executive-signed certificate of deletion. We can also provide a redacted sample manifest before signing.

Monica and Ben — looping you in to confirm operational feasibility and whether we should offer BYOK for the export bucket (helps with onshore encryption controls).

Sara, if Acme can accept a 90-day backup erasure window, we can propose the above language as a counter to your 30-day request. If that's a hard requirement for you, please highlight it and we will escalate to the infra team and legal for an exception process.

Attached: Redwood_Proposed_DPA_Redline_20260514.docx

Regards,
David Kim
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---
David Kim
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@acmecorp.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-termination data transfer & certified wipe plan

David —

Thanks for the prompt reply and the proposed language. A few points from our side after reviewing internally:

- Export timing: Acme requires a 14-day export window post-termination (we have internal cutovers that require this buffer).
- Backups: We cannot accept a 90-day deletion period for backups; we need backups containing customer production data to be purged within 30 days of transfer completion. If there are technical constraints, please enumerate them in writing.
- Geofencing: We require exported copies (and any retained ephemeral snapshots) to remain within EU physical infrastructure. We need an explicit onshore clause.
- Proof: The sample deletion manifest is good; we also need a sample job id format and a sample log extract demonstrating object tombstone creation.

Attached is Acme's redline for your counter (ACME_Redline_PostTerm.pdf). Our legal team has flagged BYOK only if Redwood can provide a clear key custody handoff process.

If Redwood cannot meet the 30-day backup deletion requirement, please propose a concrete mitigation (e.g., escrow/attestation, third-party audit, or contractual credit).

Best,
Sara Nguyen
Acme Corporation
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-termination data transfer & certified wipe plan

Sara —

Appreciate the specifics. Proposed operational compromise below and suggested contract language we can add to the DPA:

- Export window: 10 calendar days after termination notice (compromise between 7 and 14). We will provide a staging checklist and progress updates.

- Backup deletion: We will commit to deleting all live production copies within 30 days of transfer completion. For backups/snapshots, Redwood will complete irreversible deletion within 45 days of transfer completion. Rationale: snapshot chains and cross-replica GC processes require a slightly longer window; we can provide a technical annex that explains snapshot TTLs and deletion tombstone propagation.

- Geofencing: Redwood will ensure that any exported copy for Acme is written to an EU-only location provided by Acme. Redwood will not take copies outside EU for the export or long-term retention post-termination. We will also offer BYOK for the export bucket (customer supplies key; Redwood will not retain key material).

- Proof and audit: Redwood will provide (a) deletion manifest (file list + hashes); (b) internal job ids and timestamps; (c) a redacted log extract showing tombstone/object purge events; and (d) an executive-signed certificate. We will produce a sample manifest and sample log extract before signing. If Acme requires a third-party attestation, Redwood will entertain that commercially (additional SOW).

- Escalation/exception: If a legal hold is served, Redwood will notify Acme and pause deletion until Acme provides written direction. We propose including an SLA for Redwood to notify customers of retention exceptions and the expected remediation timeline.

Action items:
1) Monica to draft a short technical annex (snapshot lifecycle + timeline) for the DPA.
2) Ben to propose a commercial credit if Acme insists on 30-day backup purge and we must expend additional engineering effort for prioritized GC.
3) David to produce final compromise redline and push to DocuSign once Acme confirms acceptance.

Attached: Final_PostTerm_Compromise_20260515.docx

If that compromise works for Acme, we can update the DPA clauses and circulate a DocuSign envelope for execution.

Thanks,
David
